source.author: verg
source.text: Ac iam olim, seras posuit cum vinea frondes, frigidus et silvis aquilo decussit honorem, iam tum acer curas venientem extendit in annum rusticus et curvo Saturni dente relictam persequitur vitem attondens fingitque putando.
source.text_original: Ac iam olim, seras posuit cum vinea frondes, / frigidus et silvis aquilo decussit honorem, / iam tum acer curas venientem extendit in annum / rusticus et curvo Saturni dente relictam / persequitur vitem attondens fingitque putando.
source.text_english: And now long ago, when the vine had put forth late leaves, and the cold north wind had shaken the honor from the woods, even then the keen farmer stretches his cares into the coming year, and pursues the vine left behind by the crooked tooth of Saturn, clipping it and shaping it by pruning.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quocumque te uerteris, arator stiuam tenens alleluia decantat, sudans messor psalmis se auocat et curua attondens uitem falce uinitor aliquid Dauiticum canit.
reuse.text_original: quocumque te uerteris, arator stiuam tenens alleluia decantat, sudans messor psalmis se auocat et curua attondens uitem falce uinitor aliquid Dauiticum canit.
reuse.text_english: Wherever you turn, the ploughman, holding the plough, chants alleluia; the reaper, sweating, distracts himself with psalms; and the vintager, pruning the vine with his curved sickle, sings something of David.
